For parents and carers

Know what your child understands, and what needs practice.

KickMaths gives extra primary maths work a clear purpose. Children play short football rounds while you can inspect the maths behind the goals: independent answers, questions needing help and skills to revisit.

Create a player

A useful first session.

  1. Choose a nickname and a suitable practice year.
  2. Complete the warm-up so Coach has a starting point.
  3. Use worked steps when needed. Asking Coach for help records that support without awarding XP.
  4. Open the Parent report and look at an example question together.
  5. Return on another day so earlier facts can be checked again.

What can you see in the Parent report?

Strengths and weaker areas

A year-based chart and topic evidence show where the child has answered independently and where more support is needed.

Examples of the maths

Open a topic to see an example question, recent work and a practical next step. This makes a result easier to discuss.

How a skill becomes secure

Each skill has a visible evidence checklist. A good score or high XP level alone does not make it secure.

When a child has missed an earlier idea.

Finding a gap is useful information. Coach can check a smaller supporting skill, offer a focused drill and build back towards the original question. The child’s chosen practice year stays separate from their XP level and school year.

Dyslexia-friendly settings are easy to find.

Use the labelled Dyslexia-friendly mode button to change the font, spacing and reading background. Reduced motion can be set separately in the game. These preferences do not reduce rewards.

Read about dyslexia-friendly maths

Keep progress available.

Player progress and reports are saved in the browser used to play. Each child needs their own nickname profile. Use Backup and Restore in the grown-up area to move progress to another device, and keep a backup before clearing browser data.

Simple annual pricing.

KickMaths costs £2 per pupil per year. The same pupil price applies at home and at school. Cosmetic credits are earned in the game.

Frequently asked questions

Does KickMaths replace school teaching or tutoring?

No. It provides extra practice and information about answers given in the game. Discussion, practical activities and teacher judgement remain essential.

What makes a maths skill secure?

Most skills need at least 90% recent independent accuracy, successful work in three sessions and on three days spanning at least four days, plus enough question and method coverage. Basic facts need spaced recall; individual times tables need all multiplication and related division facts checked. The report shows the exact checklist for each skill.

Can I see results from my child’s device on my own device?

Progress is stored in the browser used to play. You can review the report there or transfer a backup to another browser. There is no automatic cloud synchronisation.
